projects.title: MaleCNS
projects.subtitle: Explore a male fly’s brain and ventral nerve cord.
projects.summary: Trace sensory-to-motor pathways through a reconstructed male fly nervous system—and inspect the dataset behind the Bitcoin demo.
projects.question: What becomes visible when the brain and nerve cord share one wiring map?
projects.does: Electron microscopy, AI-assisted reconstruction and proofreading produce cell shapes, annotations and synaptic connectivity. The collaboration compares male and female circuit anatomy and provides NeuPrint, Neuroglancer and cell-type explorers. The sampled volume includes brain, optic lobes and ventral nerve cord, with lamina and ocellar ganglion absent.
projects.boundary: This fixed anatomical map does not record ongoing neural activity or preserve the animal’s complete physiological state. The paper abstract counts 166,691 neurons; Stonkfly retains 166,700 graph nodes under its own inclusion policy. Neither number describes recording channels or model accuracy.
projects.nextTest: Which anatomical differences between male and female cell types predict a measurable difference in circuit activity?

projects.title: Eon’s embodied fly
projects.subtitle: A brain model meets a virtual body.
projects.summary: Selected outputs from a FlyWire-based brain model influence a simulated fly body, closing a loop between sensory input and movement.
projects.question: How much behavior comes from the brain model—and how much from its body controller?
projects.does: Eon combines a Shiu-style neural model, visual-system modeling and NeuroMechFly. Food cues and fictive dust produce feeding, food seeking and grooming through selected neural outputs. These signals influence imitation-trained body controllers; several brain-to-body mappings were chosen by hand.
projects.boundary: This 2026 integration is separate from the 2024 Nature circuit paper. It models a limited repertoire, with vision contributing little to the demonstrated behavior and learning largely absent. It does not establish a faithful individual brain copy. No official repository for the complete Eon integration was found in the inspected pages.
projects.nextTest: Do targeted neural perturbations change both modeled activity and behavior in ways that match an experiment on real flies?

projects.title: Stonkfly
projects.subtitle: A simulated fly connectome meets Bitcoin prices.
projects.summary: Market charts stimulate modeled fly cells; a fixed neural readout selects trades, while portfolio changes drive candidate dopamine-dependent plasticity.
projects.question: Can a connectome-constrained circuit learn a new objective?
projects.does: The public code uses MaleCNS v1.0—not a living fly. Chart brightness and color drive sensory proxies; selected descending-cell activity becomes buy, sell or hold. Portfolio gains stimulate 15 modeled PAM11 cells, losses two PPL101 cells. A candidate rule changes 7,835 existing KC-to-MBON connections. Paper mode starts with a simulated $100 balance.
projects.boundary: The author reports no demonstrated profitable learning. Recorded validation used paper trades and simulated order tests; a funded live-account run was not verified here. Feedback includes price changes while holding, so it does not isolate the last trade’s effect. Artificial dopamine-cell stimulation is not evidence of pleasure or consciousness.
projects.nextTest: Does contingent feedback outperform shuffled feedback and frozen weights on unseen price sequences, after fees and identical trade limits?

projects.title: MICrONS
projects.subtitle: Link mouse cortical wiring to visual responses.
projects.summary: Explore a mouse cortical volume where electron-microscopy wiring is matched to recorded activity and predictive visual-response models.
projects.question: How are a cell’s connections related to what it responds to?
projects.does: MICrONS combines calcium imaging of roughly 75,000 neurons with an electron-microscopy reconstruction containing more than 200,000 cells and about half a billion synapses. Researchers can query connectivity, inspect cell morphology, and connect a subset of reconstructed cells to their visual responses. Companion work uses neural-network response models to test which functional similarities predict connections.
projects.boundary: The cubic-millimetre dataset comes from one mouse visual-cortex volume. It is neither a complete mouse brain nor a human brain. Its functional “digital twin” predicts selected visual responses; it does not reproduce every cell mechanism or all behavior.
projects.nextTest: Which proposed wiring rule still predicts connections after accounting for cell type, spatial proximity and held-out stimuli?

projects.title: FlyVis
projects.subtitle: Infer visual responses from wiring and a task.
projects.summary: A connectome-constrained network learns visual motion and predicts neural responses that can be checked against physiology.
projects.question: Can anatomy plus a useful task recover neural response properties?
projects.does: The network covers 64 cell types in the fly motion pathway. Researchers optimize unknown neuronal and synaptic parameters for motion estimation, then compare predicted responses with measurements from 26 studies. Public PyTorch code, pretrained models and notebooks make the assumptions inspectable.
projects.boundary: This is a visual-system model, not a complete brain. Its predictions depend on measured wiring, task choice and optimization; they do not show that anatomy alone specifies every neural dynamic.
projects.nextTest: Which response properties remain accurate under unfamiliar visual stimuli or a targeted perturbation of the modeled circuit?

projects.title: DishBrain / CL1
projects.subtitle: Put living neurons in a software-defined feedback loop.
projects.summary: Cultured neural networks receive electrical inputs, produce recorded outputs and interact with a software-defined environment.
projects.question: What can a living culture change through feedback?
projects.does: The DishBrain experiment connected human-derived or mouse cortical cultures to a high-density electrode array and a simplified Pong environment. The authors reported improved performance under structured feedback relative to control conditions. Cortical Labs now documents the CL1 platform and programming interfaces for reading spikes, scheduling stimulation and building real-time feedback experiments.
projects.boundary: The experiment does not establish general intelligence, human-like understanding or subjective experience, despite the original title's use of “sentience.” CL1's product availability does not itself validate therapeutic benefits or a computational advantage over conventional hardware on matched workloads.
projects.nextTest: Does adaptation survive held-out task conditions, no-feedback controls and changes in the external encoder and decoder?

projects.title: FlyWire
projects.subtitle: Explore the adult female fly brain.
projects.summary: Automated reconstruction, community proofreading and annotation turn an adult female fly brain into an explorable wiring graph.
projects.question: How can a brain-wide map guide a specific circuit question?
projects.does: The published reconstruction describes 139,255 proofread neurons and approximately 54.5 million chemical synapses between reconstructed neurons. Cell annotations and 3D tools help trace pathways across the central brain and optic lobes. Public releases identify their version so analyses can be reproduced.
projects.boundary: This is one fixed specimen, without the contiguous ventral nerve cord. It is not a recording of ongoing activity or a functional emulation. The later reconstruction count differs from the earlier FlyWire v630 subset used by the Shiu model.
projects.nextTest: Which predicted pathway remains robust when edge thresholds, reconstruction uncertainty and alternative routes are considered?

projects.title: CEBRA
projects.subtitle: Compare neural activity in a learned coordinate system.
projects.summary: Compress high-dimensional recordings into representations that can be compared across sessions, animals and recording methods.
projects.question: Does shared structure survive a change of session or recording method?
projects.does: CEBRA learns compact representations of time-series data using temporal structure and, when appropriate, measured behavioral or stimulus variables. The paper demonstrates neural-behavior alignment, consistency across recordings, position and movement decoding, and identification of viewed movie frames. Tutorials show how to fit models and test consistency across repeated runs or datasets.
projects.boundary: An appealing embedding is not proof of a causal neural mechanism. Behavior labels shape the representation. The movie demonstration concerns recorded responses to known stimuli; it does not establish unrestricted reconstruction of thoughts, dreams or unseen experiences.
projects.nextTest: Do the same features survive held-out data, repeated training and a comparison against time-only and shuffled-label baselines?

projects.title: ZAPBench
projects.subtitle: Predict future activity in a larval zebrafish brain.
projects.summary: Measured calcium traces and held-out tests let researchers compare how well models forecast brain activity.
projects.question: Can a model predict what a recorded neural population will do next?
projects.does: The benchmark uses whole-brain light-sheet calcium imaging during visual stimulation. Reference time-series and volumetric models forecast future signals from observed history. Public data, notebooks and interactive comparisons make prediction errors inspectable.
projects.boundary: Calcium fluorescence is an optical measurement, not an electrode recording or a direct spike count. Forecasting these recorded conditions does not establish unrestricted behavior or faithful whole-brain emulation. Its public activity data and Fire&Wire’s draft structural snapshots have different access terms.
projects.nextTest: Does a model generalize to unfamiliar stimulus conditions and outperform simple temporal baselines over longer forecast horizons?

projects.title: NeuroMechFly / FlyGym
projects.subtitle: Put a controller inside a physically simulated fly.
projects.summary: An articulated fly body with sensory feedback helps researchers test how computation and movement interact.
projects.question: What changes when a neural controller must move a body?
projects.does: The framework models adult female fly anatomy derived from micro-CT, joints, contact forces, adhesion and sensory inputs. The v2 paper demonstrates learned and biologically inspired controllers for navigation and stabilization. Public code, tutorials and a body viewer provide several starting points.
projects.boundary: A body simulator does not automatically supply a complete connectome-derived nervous system. Plausible movement can result from a trained or hand-designed controller. Current FlyGym 2.x differs from the paper-era 1.x API; the browser body viewer does not run Eon’s complete brain–body model.
projects.nextTest: Does a proposed controller still work after changes in terrain, sensory delay or body mechanics?

projects.title: Brain-Score
projects.subtitle: Turn brain-like AI claims into specific tests.
projects.summary: Run computational models against neural and behavioral benchmarks, and inspect where their predictions break down.
projects.question: Which experiment distinguishes two models with similar average scores?
projects.does: Brain-Score gives models standardized experimental interfaces and compares their predictions with biological measurements. Scores summarize alignment within particular datasets, metrics and tasks; the site also exposes benchmark-level results. Its plugin system lets researchers contribute models or new experiments, including tests designed to reveal weaknesses in otherwise successful models.
projects.boundary: A high aggregate score is not a percentage of human intelligence or proof of the brain's mechanism. Scores depend on the selected benchmarks, noise ceilings and model-to-data mapping. They do not establish general competence outside the measured domain.
projects.nextTest: Which new behavioral or neural experiment separates models that look equally good on the current benchmark average?

projects.title: Brainoware
projects.subtitle: Use an organoid’s dynamics as a computational reservoir.
projects.summary: An experimental hybrid system uses a brain organoid's changing electrical responses as part of a computing pipeline.
projects.question: Which useful features come from living tissue dynamics?
projects.does: Brainoware sends patterned electrical stimulation into a brain organoid through a high-density multielectrode array and records the resulting activity. The authors use these nonlinear, history-dependent responses in a reservoir-computing framework and report speech-related classification and nonlinear-equation prediction demonstrations. The project links the dynamics of living tissue with conventional electronic input and output processing.
projects.boundary: These narrow experimental tasks do not demonstrate conversational understanding, general intelligence or a whole-brain simulation. The paper does not establish a deployable replacement for GPUs or a matched, end-to-end energy advantage including tissue maintenance and readout equipment.
projects.nextTest: How much of the task performance comes from organoid adaptation rather than the external preprocessing and readout, and does it reproduce across cultures?

projects.title: BANC
projects.subtitle: Trace circuits across a female brain and nerve cord.
projects.summary: A brain-and-cord reconstruction exposes paths linking sensory inputs, ascending and descending signals, and motor-related circuitry.
projects.question: How is control distributed between the brain and nerve cord?
projects.does: Serial electron microscopy and proofreading produce the v888 female reconstruction. The paper combines backbone-proofread and roughly proofread neurons and analyzes connectivity-based influence across the nervous system. It includes brain and ventral nerve cord, with lamina and ocellar ganglion absent.
projects.boundary: An anatomical influence analysis is not a validated functional emulation. Detected pre–post links across the volume use a different denominator from synapses between identified reconstructed neurons; raw totals should not be ranked without their inclusion rules.
projects.nextTest: Do predicted influence pathways identify perturbations that change measured movement or neural activity?

projects.title: Shiu’s fly brain model
projects.subtitle: Use a whole-brain model to test specific circuits.
projects.summary: A simplified FlyWire-based model generates experimentally testable predictions about feeding and antennal grooming.
projects.question: Which circuit functions can be predicted from measured wiring?
projects.does: The model represents 127,400 proofread neurons from FlyWire v630 with leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics. Synapse counts and predicted neurotransmitters constrain connections; explicit physiological assumptions and a tuned synaptic gain complete the model. Circuit predictions are compared with experimental interventions and measurements.
projects.boundary: The paper reports 91% agreement across 164 circuit predictions, or 84% excluding a largely negative optogenetic screen. These are not whole-animal behavioral accuracy scores; a general 95%-motor-accuracy claim is unsupported. The study does not provide Eon’s later body integration or all biological learning and modulatory mechanisms.
projects.nextTest: Do predictions survive changes in assumed synaptic strength and outperform simpler circuit baselines on new interventions?

projects.title: POYO
projects.subtitle: Reuse a decoder when the recorded neurons change.
projects.summary: Represent spikes as tokens so one neural-population model can learn from many recording sessions.
projects.question: Can one decoder transfer across populations with different neuron identities?
projects.does: POYO tokenizes spike identity and timing, then uses attention to build a shared representation of population activity. Its reported training subset includes 158 sessions from seven nonhuman primates. The model can be adapted to held-out sessions with little labeled data even when neuron identities do not correspond across recordings. The project explains spike and behavior-query tokens interactively.
projects.boundary: Adaptation across these motor-related datasets is not universal decoding across every species, behavior or recording modality. The training subset differs from the larger curated corpus on the project page. This is a predictive model, not a mechanistic copy of an individual brain.
projects.nextTest: How much labeled recalibration is needed after electrode drift, and how does transfer compare with a strong session-specific decoder?

projects.title: IBL Brain-Wide Map
projects.subtitle: Compare a common task across regions and laboratories.
projects.summary: Compare neural activity across laboratories and brain regions using a shared mouse decision-making experiment.
projects.question: Does a neural result transfer across laboratories and animals?
projects.does: IBL standardized a visual decision task and combined recordings across 12 laboratories. Release documentation describes 699 probe insertions from 139 mice: 621,733 spike-sorted units, of which 75,708 passed the stated good-quality selection. Open tools connect neural activity with stimuli, choices, response times and tracked movements, allowing researchers to benchmark analyses across sessions and regions.
projects.boundary: The map pools recordings across animals and sessions. Those unit counts are not simultaneously recorded channels or a count of unique tracked neurons in one brain. Brain-wide sampling does not measure every neuron or establish causal decision circuitry by itself.
projects.nextTest: Does a decoder or latent model generalize to a held-out lab, animal and brain region without depending on lab-specific artifacts?

projects.title: Fish Fire&Wire
projects.subtitle: Align neural activity and wiring in the same zebrafish.
projects.summary: Activity imaging followed by electron microscopy links the same cells’ responses with their anatomical connections.
projects.question: Does measured wiring improve predictions of measured activity?
projects.does: The Fish2 project combines light-sheet imaging, serial electron microscopy, synapse detection and cross-modality registration. Its scope includes the brain and peripheral sensory/motor structures of a six-day-old larval zebrafish. Reconstruction and proofreading remain ongoing.
projects.boundary: The inspected project is an unfinished draft, not a finalized peer-reviewed connectome. Structural snapshots require a research-group request and carry publication restrictions; consult the current terms. Fish2 is distinct from the separate seven-day-old Fish1 structural atlas, and is not a fly dataset.
projects.nextTest: Does adding verified connections improve held-out activity prediction over a model using recordings alone?

projects.title: BrainLM
projects.subtitle: Pretrain on fMRI, then test transfer to a new analysis.
projects.summary: A foundation-model experiment that learns reusable representations by predicting masked portions of fMRI time series.
projects.question: Does broad pretraining help a new neural-data task?
projects.does: BrainLM uses self-supervised masked prediction on 6,700 hours of fMRI recordings. The paper evaluates forecasting, prediction of participant variables and transfer to external cohorts. The authors' repository includes inference notebooks, preprocessing instructions and links to pretrained models, allowing researchers to examine whether a shared representation helps a particular downstream analysis.
projects.boundary: BOLD fMRI is an indirect, relatively slow measurement of neural activity. Predicting masked data or study variables does not validate an individual clinical diagnosis, decode arbitrary thoughts or reproduce the brain's causal mechanisms. UK Biobank training data require separate approved access.
projects.nextTest: Does an advantage persist across scanners, preprocessing pipelines and held-out sites after controlling for age and other confounds?

projects.title: OpenWorm / c302
projects.subtitle: Connect a worm nervous-system model to a body.
projects.summary: Configurable neural models and a physical body simulation make whole-organism modeling assumptions visible.
projects.question: Which level of biological detail is needed to explain behavior?
projects.does: The c302 framework generates NeuroML nervous-system models with different levels of biophysical detail. OpenWorm publishes integration code linking neural activity, muscles and the Sibernetic body simulation, supporting experiments on the interaction between circuit dynamics and movement.
projects.boundary: A runnable integration is not a validated reproduction of every natural behavior. The 2018 papers describe their publication-era system; current repository features require separate evaluation. Neither establishes an exact individual mind or a complete digital organism.
projects.nextTest: Which observed behaviors require extra biophysical detail, and which survive a simpler model with the same wiring?

projects.title: FinalSpark Neuroplatform
projects.subtitle: Access recording and stimulation through a remote API.
projects.summary: A maintained wet-lab platform exposes neural recording and stimulation through a remote Python interface.
projects.question: Can the same feedback experiment reproduce across independent cultures?
projects.does: FinalSpark combines organoid cultures, electrode recording and stimulation, environmental support and remote software. Its 2024 paper demonstrates programmable electrophysiology and feedback experiments. Public documentation explains access and API use, while the current company page offers shared or dedicated hardware access and a request route for recorded datasets.
projects.boundary: The authors explicitly say their single illustrated feedback experiment cannot establish that feedback caused the observed change in firing. The platform paper does not demonstrate an LLM trained on organoids or a measured replacement for GPU computing. Public documentation does not mean unrestricted free hardware access.
projects.nextTest: Which stimulation protocol produces a reproducible, task-specific change across independent cultures beyond spontaneous drift and control stimulation?

projects.title: DOOMFLY
projects.subtitle: A connectome experiment inside a game.
projects.summary: ViZDoom frames drive modeled fly sensory cells, and selected neural activity becomes game controls.
projects.question: What would distinguish learned survival from a lucky round?
projects.does: A retained MaleCNS simulation uses engineered sensory and action adapters. Game damage stimulates modeled dopamine cells; candidate plasticity changes existing KC-to-MBON connections. Neural state and memory can persist across game deaths.
projects.boundary: The current v6 README reports failed visual, conditioning and survival validation gates. Synaptic changes or individual longer rounds do not establish learned survival. The browser viewer is not evidence that the full neural model executes in the browser.
projects.nextTest: Does the plastic model improve survival across held-out rounds against frozen-weight and shuffled-feedback controls?

projects.title: Neuromatch NeuroAI
projects.subtitle: Learn by comparing biological and artificial systems.
projects.summary: An open curriculum for turning brain-and-AI questions into small coding experiments and research projects.
projects.question: How do you turn a NeuroAI idea into a small, testable experiment?
projects.does: The NeuroAI course combines computational neuroscience and deep learning around generalization, comparing tasks and networks, microcircuits, architectures and learning rules. The open course book contains explanations, videos and coding exercises. A generalization tutorial asks learners to inspect recurrent-model activity and behavior, including what was already present before training.
projects.boundary: Completing a tutorial does not establish a new biological theory or validate a clinical application. Course examples illustrate ways to reason and test models; their results depend on the exercise assumptions and chosen datasets.
projects.nextTest: Can a proposed shared learning principle predict a failure case in both a neural dataset and an artificial model?
